title: The Law of Least Effort
coreMove: Redraw the path so the desired action is the lower-friction default.
sourcePressure: Behavior often follows the path of least resistance, so good habit design reduces friction for the desired action and increases friction for the unwanted one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using ease as laziness rather than as a deliberately designed path of least resistance.

hook: starting with a definition of least effort
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a rural nurse placing vaccination coolers beside the intake desk
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic director improving same-visit vaccination rates
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether lower friction makes the right action easier than deferral
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse can vaccinate before the family leaves because the cooler and consent pad are already in the intake path
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a vaccine cooler tucked under an intake counter

exampleSpecs.domain: a calligrapher leaving practice nibs soaking next to the sink
exampleSpecs.audience: a hobbyist who skips cleanup and then avoids practice
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether reducing setup drag protects tomorrow practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: clean nibs wait in a labeled tray, so the next session starts with ink instead of scraping
exampleSpecs.firstImage: silver nibs drying in a porcelain tray

exampleSpecs.domain: a theater stage manager taping cable paths before rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a crew lead reducing repeated trip hazards
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the low-resistance path is physically drawn on the floor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: actors follow the taped route without instruction because it is easier than stepping around loose cables
exampleSpecs.firstImage: bright tape running across a black stage floor

exampleSpecs.domain: a beekeeper moving the hive tool to the first box handle
exampleSpecs.audience: a beekeeper who abandons inspections when setup sprawls
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the needed action is made the easiest next reach
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she grips the box handle and finds the hive tool already clipped there, so the inspection begins
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a hive tool clipped to a painted box handle

exampleSpecs.domain: a college dining hall making fruit the first tray item
exampleSpecs.audience: a nutrition director changing defaults without preaching
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether convenience changes selection before preference is debated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: students take fruit because tongs and bowls appear before dessert, proving path beats posters
exampleSpecs.firstImage: green pears stacked before the entree line

exampleSpecs.domain: a mailroom clerk pre-sorting return labels by route color
exampleSpecs.audience: a clerk overwhelmed by end-of-day parcels
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether friction removal changes repeated behavior
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: colored label bins cut four handoffs, and the clerk notices fewer parcels left after cutoff
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored label bins lined beneath a sorting shelf

skillTargets: identify friction points in a behavior path
redesign defaults toward the desired action
raise friction without relying on shame

tryThisNowSpec: Lower the friction on one good action by one physical step, and raise the friction on one unwanted action by one physical step.
